name: אֲבִידָן
gloss: my father is judge; or my father has judged
summary: The prince of Benjamin in the wilderness, son of Gideoni: he stood with Moses and Aaron at the numbering, brought Benjamin’s offering on the ninth day of the altar’s dedication, and led Benjamin’s host when the camps set out from Sinai (Num 1:11; 7:60; 10:24). The name joins אָבִי, “my father”, to דָּן, “judged, judge”, the word of Rachel’s “God has judged me” (Gen 30:6), and says of God what Psalm 68 says, “a father of the fatherless and a judge (דַּיַּן) of widows is God” (Psa 68:6).

evidence.note: “Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, אֲבִידָן son of Gideoni.”
The prince of the sons of Benjamin in the camp of Ephraim.
On the ninth day, the prince of the sons of Benjamin brings his offering (and 7:65).
אֲבִי יְתוֹמִים וְדַיַּן אַלְמָנוֹת אֱלֹהִים: God as father and as judge in one line, the name’s two parts.
דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים, “God has judged me”: the verb whose form ends the name, said of God taking up a cause.

note: BDB files the name under אבה (a.ae.ag, among the av entry’s words); it is linked here for its distinctive second part, as Eliab is linked to av for its second part. The ־ִי may be the suffix “my” or a joining vowel (“the father is judge”); compare אֲבִינָדָב and אֲבִיעֶזֶר. דָּן may be the perfect, “my father has judged”, or the participle, “my father is judge”.
